entrada.titulo: Secure and trusted data sharing in smart healthcare using blockchain and IoT integration

perfil_anterior.problema: prevent data from having a single point of failure
perfil_anterior.solucao: Integrates an Interplanetary File System (IPFS) with the Blockchain network to reduce blockchain network overload and enhance healthcare systems’ scalability and storage capacity
perfil_anterior.avaliacao: The results show that public healthcare systems based on the Blockchain considerably boost efficiency and performance by integrating IPFS.

3 System model
Processing real-time healthcare data, timely patient monitoring, and providing health -
care services are challenging for healthcare providers worldwide [ 30, 31]. Although 
most existing Blockchain-integrated IoT systems provide smart healthcare systems, as 
the number of connected healthcare devices grows, the system’s access to, processing, 
and storage of healthcare data slows down. The inability to deliver continuous, real-time 
patient care is a major concern for many healthcare facilities. Patients may get worse 
or possibly die if they do not receive the best possible care immediately. To address 
the shortcomings of current Blockchain-integrated IoT healthcare systems, we have 
proposed an IPFS-integrated Blockchain-IoT healthcare system. Figure  1. depicts the 
proposed framework, which is secure, interoperable, and scalable for healthcare organi -
zations. It integrates Blockchain, IoT, and IPFS (Table 1).
3.1 Framework description
In this system, real-time patient care is prioritized above all else. Still, strong privacy, 
security, and scalability solutions for accessing, processing, transferring, and storing 
healthcare data are also paramount. Each “block" in the Blockchain healthcare system 
is a timestamped, cryptographically linked, distributed, and immutable set of records. 
The proposed system employs smart contracts built on the Ethereum platform to check 
if IoT devices adhere to pre-defined privacy policies and other limitations. Device access 
permissions are granted to devices via a smart contract-defined access management 
and authentication method. All healthcare IoT devices used in this framework fall into 
secured and unsecured categories. Unsecured IoT devices are cheap and vulnerable 
and cannot execute privacy policies and agreements. These devices are connected via 
a device proxy. The device proxy authorises these gadgets to the system and monitors
